analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/delta-complete-checkpoints.md, lines 1-3) and a short addition to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines 526-528, plus a date bump at line 3). No source code was supplied, so no security controls were modified in the supplied evidence.

The docs describe a behavior change in the SSD prefix cache (T-041, TB-007, A-001). Qwen 3.8 native recurrent complete checkpoints are now written as deltas of a restored file, with a restore reading the chain forward. The changelog adds an opt-out env var, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS=0.

The delta-chain implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so the following cannot be verified here:
- Whether each delta file remains independently AES-GCM authenticated, with the manifest binding exact tokens, scope/cacheSalt and parent identity.
- Whether the parent link uses an HMAC-keyed tag rather than a raw prefix hash on disk.
- Whether TTL and LRU eviction of a parent invalidates dependent deltas, or lets a delta outlive its chain.
- Whether a chain restore has bounded length and read scratch, and whether cross-scope or cross-tenant chain linking is prevented.
- Whether the removal of a parent from a chain leaves the sliding TTL (30 minutes) and the SEC-035 acceptance unchanged.
- Whether the write-ledger accounting for deltas stays correct.

None of these is a demonstrated regression. I raise them as unverified contracts, not findings. The next review pass should examine the actual code changes (SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Write/Read, CompleteCheckpointTransfer and the DBK3 format) for these properties against T-041 mitigations (c) and (d).

No threat-model update is needed from the docs alone. The delta-chain at-rest layout and its parent-reference metadata may warrant a T-041 update once code is reviewed.
